human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: horizontal_push is a loose label. The load is held up over the shoulders and the motion is scapular protraction. shoulder_raise or a similar family might fit as well or better. Labels do not change the traced muscles, and no family cleanly describes protraction.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally consider shoulder_raise alongside or instead of horizontal_push in a future revision.

non_blocking_findings.finding: Rotator cuff muscles (infraspinatus, supraspinatus, subscapularis) are not engaged. They would likely co-contract to centre the humeral head while the dumbbells are held at about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion. This is a minor omission, and shoulder_position_hold already covers the main isometric shoulder load.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally add glenohumeral_stabilization if the rotator cuff is considered meaningfully engaged.

model_reviewer.summary: The frames and instructions show a bilateral incline-bench dumbbell movement. The arms stay straight and locked while the shoulders rise off the bench, which is scapular protraction. The definition captures this with scapulothoracic_joint/protraction as the sole primary action, so serratus anterior is primary (1.0) and pectoralis minor a synergist (0.5). Grip and wrist_stability fit a load held in the hands. shoulder_position_hold and elbow_joint_integrity credit the held shoulder flexion and the locked elbows without listing a moving elbow or glenohumeral joint. Bilateral laterality, an empty one_sided_limbs and an open-chain label are all supported by the frames. The resulting muscle pattern is plausible, and the remaining points are label or minor-weighting matters.
